Introduced this flag here to fix flaky test runs and isolate them from each other since otherwise they would be using the same DBus session.

Since the tests are pretty fast, i do not think it will be an issue to run them sequentially. 

Alternative would be `dbus-run-session` but that inroduces another indirection and makes it less straightforward to run tests manually.
Let's look into why it is not working in the parallel case. It should work.
Yes, please check the actual reason for the test failure.
I did multiple scans of the code to figure out difference between testSoftwareAssociationRunning and testSoftwareAssociationActivating, they looks exactly same or am i missing something here?

Please create one helper function and pass some in_args which can help you to do some decision making. Looks like most of the code is same in all 3 helper functions and with some in_args, it can easily be folded into one.

Removed `busName` and `objPathCurrentSoftware` from each of those testcases.

The rest is just forming the client (which is the same but has a fairly verbose template which i did not see anyone actually write down).

For that reason i declare the client in the testcase.

The remainder is just the assertions which are unique for each testcase.

The `ctx.request_stop` is something i left in there so folks can just comment that out when debugging some test case.

Let me know if i should compact the code further.

Fold testSoftwareAssociationActivating and testSoftwareAssociationRunning into one function testSoftwareAssociation and pass the association name as in_arg from caller. As i see the only difference between 2 functions is the association name so lets pass it as input to new function testSoftwareAssociation.

@alexander.hansen@9elements.com Can you please check why you need this NOLINTNEXTLINE and create a followup patch to fix this if its an actual warning. We can discuss on this thread once you have a trace for this warning.
For now, i am merging this patch since all other comments have been resolved.

#### my nolint here was not required after all

Raised https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/+/84538
to drop the NOLINT.

Apparently it was not required, not sure if it's due to clang update or code restructuring in later revisions of this patch.

#### general shape of these errors

Generally these errors always take the same shape for me,
clang-tidy detects that stdexec is dereferencing an optional 

```

```

without checking. 
I'm still unsure why it triggers in some cases but not in others.

The example log is from bios updater where we have the same NOLINT.

#### code block causing the issue

The code block for reference

```
  425         template <sender _Awaitable>
  426             requires __scheduler_provider<_Context>
  427         auto await_transform(_Awaitable&& __awaitable) noexcept
  428             -> decltype(auto)
  429         {
  430             // TODO: If we have a complete-where-it-starts query then we can
  431             // optimize this to avoid the reschedule
  432             return as_awaitable(
  433                 continues_on(static_cast<_Awaitable&&>(__awaitable),
A>434                              get_scheduler(*__context_)),
  435                 *this);
  436         }
```

#### upstream workaround

It looks like in the upstream code they used some workaround to hide this from clang
https://github.com/NVIDIA/stdexec/blob/138e136fa4b93e7e096a4968eaac1b0c94f0d255/include/exec/task.hpp#L390
```

#ifndef __clang_analyzer__
        template <sender _Awaitable>
          requires __scheduler_provider<_Context>
        auto await_transform(_Awaitable&& __awaitable) noexcept -> decltype(auto) {
          // TODO: If we have a complete-where-it-starts query then we can optimize
          // this to avoid the reschedule
          return stdexec::as_awaitable(
            continues_on(static_cast<_Awaitable&&>(__awaitable), get_scheduler(*__context_)),
            *this);
        }

        template <class _Scheduler>
          requires __scheduler_provider<_Context>
        auto await_transform(__reschedule_coroutine_on::__wrap<_Scheduler> __box) noexcept
          -> decltype(auto) {
          if (!std::exchange(__rescheduled_, true)) {
            // Create a cleanup action that transitions back onto the current scheduler:
            auto __sched = get_scheduler(*__context_);
            auto __cleanup_task = at_coroutine_exit(schedule, std::move(__sched));
            // Insert the cleanup action into the head of the continuation chain by making
            // direct calls to the cleanup task's awaiter member functions. See type
            // _cleanup_task in at_coroutine_exit.hpp:
            __cleanup_task.await_suspend(__coro::coroutine_handle<__promise>::from_promise(*this));
            (void) __cleanup_task.await_resume();
          }
          __context_->set_scheduler(__box.__sched_);
          return stdexec::as_awaitable(schedule(__box.__sched_), *this);
        }
#endif
```

we can blame to see the commit introducing this guard

https://github.com/NVIDIA/stdexec/commit/41f673ee50ce5f3b652522b95a5a35c58cba9eb6

and the relevant PR

https://github.com/NVIDIA/stdexec/pull/1551

#### thoughts

IMO the fix looks sus because it hides the actual issue.

If the code works without the section they compiled out, why not remove it entirely?

If the code does not work without these functions, then why not put the NOLINT at that location, so library users do not have to deal with it.
